Enterprise Risk Management Framework: Global Standard

Regulator: EUR_LEX
Jurisdiction: EU
Publication Date: 2018-10-01
Effective Date: 2019-01-01
Source URL: https://www.iso.org/standard/65694.html
License: ISO Copyright - Reproduced with permission

Section 1: Governance
The board of directors is responsible for the overall risk appetite statement. A Chief Risk Officer (CRO) must be appointed to oversee the risk management function.

Section 2: Risk Identification
Risks shall be identified through quarterly assessments across all business units. Risks are categorized as Operational, Credit, Market, or Liquidity.

Section 3: Mitigation Strategies
Mitigation strategies must be documented and reviewed annually. Strategies include insurance, hedging, or risk avoidance.

Section 4: Monitoring and Reporting
The CRO shall provide a monthly risk report to the board. Reports must highlight breaches of risk limits.

Section 5: Audit and Review
Internal audit shall review the risk framework every two years to ensure alignment with global standards.

Section 6: Compliance and Enforcement
Non-compliance with risk limits will trigger an immediate review by the compliance committee.

Section 7: Materiality Thresholds
A risk is deemed material if it exceeds 5% of the total capital reserve.

Section 8: Reporting Timelines
Material breaches must be reported to the regulator within 48 hours.

Section 9: Documentation
All risk assessments must be signed by the unit head and the CRO.

Section 10: Training
Annual risk management training is mandatory for all employees with decision-making authority.
